title: A backup is a file-level snapshot of the store artifact taken without downtime
description: The backup procedure produces a self-contained artifact (a copy of the SQLite file, an engine-native snapshot, or the equivalent) that, when opened by a compatible build, boots to the same schema version and holds the same committed rows as the source store at the snapshot moment. The procedure runs against a live store: no request quiescence, no consumer freeze, no application shutdown. The backup runner emits a backupCheckpoint event on the store's event log with the artifact path and the ISO-8601 completion timestamp.
rationale: A backup story that requires downtime is a backup story the operator will skip until it is too late. A file-level snapshot inherits the durability posture of the underlying engine (WAL checkpointing for SQLite, replication slots for Postgres) and turns 'do we have a recent backup' into a stat call on the artifact path. The event on completion is what makes 'when did the last snapshot land' answerable from the log without a filesystem walk.
